title: Fix concurrency issues
description:
The crash check probed each in-progress message's lock file with the full busy timeout, while holding the main DB lock. With N active workers every poll held the lock for N times the timeout, so other clients failed. Probe lock files with no timeout instead.

Also use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for all writes, to avoid deadlocks between deferred transactions and to let readers run during writes. The message lock files stay BEGIN EXCLUSIVE: a weaker lock does not block readers, so live workers would look crashed.

Superseeds #29. Closes #28.

title: close #28: fix concurrency issues and deadlocks
description:
This is my take at #28, which partially revisits #26. This PR basically 

- makes `do_db_execute` take the lock, because every call to it is a write;
- makes `publish` take the lock, same reason;
- substitutes `EXCLUSIVE` locks with `IMMEDIATE` locks.

This works very well for my use case in #28, but please take a look to ensure that I'm not missing something. Compared to master, tests are much quicker now, but two tests fail, which I believe are spurious errors due to the fact that IMMEDIATE locks can coexist with readers:

```
══ Failed tests ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
── Failure (test-db.R:79:3): db_lock ───────────────────────────────────────────
`db_query(con3, "SELECT * FROM meta")` did not throw an error.
── Failure (test-db.R:82:3): db_lock ───────────────────────────────────────────
`db_query(con2, "SELECT * FROM meta")` did not throw an error.

[ FAIL 2 | WARN 0 | SKIP 11 | PASS 173 ]

```

title: fix #25: publish several messages in one transaction
description:
Example:

```r
library(liteq)

task <- function(db) {
  library(liteq)
  q <- ensure_queue("jobs", db = db)
  msg <- consume(q)
  out <- msg$title
  Sys.sleep(10)
  ack(msg)
  out
}

db <- tempfile()
q <- ensure_queue("jobs", db = db)

n <- 10
workers <- replicate(n, callr::r_bg(task, list(db=db)))

publish(q, letters[1:n], rep("something", n))

Sys.sleep(15)
sort(sapply(workers, function(x) x$get_result()))
#>  [1] "a" "b" "c" "d" "e" "f" "g" "h" "i" "j"
```
